theBigPicture: Hurricane Isaias slammed into the US Gulf Coast, killing two people and leaving roughly 800,000 homes and businesses without power, while an attack on Saudi Arabia's main airport showed the Middle East war is now hitting everyday travel hubs. In Washington, a controversial deal easing sanctions on Russian diesel has triggered a public feud with Ukraine's leader, even as Russian strikes killed 15 people in Ukraine. Despite all the turmoil, financial markets remain calm — which is quietly good news for your retirement accounts.

householdImpact.energyAndFuel: Oil prices remain high because of the ongoing war, with crude trading between roughly $96 and $125 a barrel, so expect continued pain at the gas pump. Natural gas prices are normal, meaning home heating and cooking bills should stay steady for now.
householdImpact.borrowingAndMortgages: Financial markets are calm and lending conditions are easy, which is helping keep mortgage and auto loan rates from spiking. Credit card rates remain high, so paying down balances is still the smartest money move.
householdImpact.groceriesAndSupplyChain: High fuel costs make it more expensive to truck food to stores, keeping grocery bills elevated. The US deal to release Russian diesel could eventually ease some shipping costs, but war-related disruptions are still pushing prices up.
householdImpact.jobsAndSavings: Stock markets are steady, which is good news for 401(k)s and retirement accounts. Businesses are operating in a stable environment, but persistently high fuel prices can squeeze company budgets and slow hiring in transportation-heavy industries.

globalFlashpoints.summary: President Trump said it is 'time for Ukraine to get a new president' after Ukraine's leader criticized a US deal easing sanctions on Russian diesel, while Russian strikes killed 15 people — including three children — in the city of Zaporizhzhia.
A Houthi attack injured dozens and forced Saudi Arabia to shut its main Riyadh airport, as the wider war involving Iran keeps striking civilian infrastructure and oil facilities across the region.
The aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln returned home after a grueling 321-day deployment supporting the Iran war, with no new flashpoints reported in the Pacific.

India detained over 2,000 protesters to block a youth-led rally against its election chief, anti-migrant riots flared for a second day in South Africa, and thousands marched in support of Palestinians in London and Berlin.

topStories.headline: Hurricane Isaias Knocks Out Power to 800,000 Across the Southeast
topStories.whyItMatters: Two people are dead and hundreds of thousands are in the dark, with officials warning of spinoff tornadoes as the storm moves inland. If you live in Florida, Alabama, or nearby states, expect outages and travel headaches to linger for days.

topStories.headline: Dozens Injured as Attack Forces Saudi Arabia to Shut Its Main Airport
topStories.whyItMatters: The strike on Riyadh's international airport shows the Middle East conflict is now disrupting major global travel hubs. Travelers with flights through the region should brace for cancellations and delays.

topStories.headline: Trump's Russian Diesel Deal Sparks Public Feud With Ukraine's Leader
topStories.whyItMatters: The deal could help lower fuel prices in the US, but critics — including Ukraine's president — say it hands Moscow money to fund the war. It is driving a very public rift between Washington and Kyiv at a sensitive moment.

topStories.headline: She Survived Her Own Execution — and the Debate Is Back On
topStories.whyItMatters: Tennessee inmate Christa Pike survived two rounds of lethal injection drugs and has now returned to prison, renewing scrutiny of how America carries out executions. The case lands just as executions worldwide are on the rise.

topStories.headline: India Locks Down Delhi and Detains 2,000 to Stop Youth Protest
topStories.whyItMatters: A satirical youth movement demanding the election chief's resignation has become the biggest domestic challenge to India's government in years. The sweeping crackdown could fuel even larger protests ahead.

topStories.headline: Nine Dead, Including Children, in Pennsylvania Mass Shooting
topStories.whyItMatters: The massacre in Erie is among the deadliest US mass shootings this year. Authorities say the suspect is dead and there is no ongoing threat to the public.

whatWeAreWatching: Power restoration efforts after Hurricane Isaias, plus the risk of spinoff tornadoes as the storm pushes further inland over the next few days.
Whether Saudi Arabia reopens Riyadh's main airport and how it responds to escalating Houthi attacks on its own soil.
Political fallout from the US-Russia diesel deal and Trump's call for new leadership in Ukraine, which could reshape Western support for the war.
The US midterm elections next month, where forecasters increasingly expect Republicans to lose control of the House of Representatives.
Rising tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea after a reported border incursion, with Eritrea now asking the United Nations to step in.
